title: Join the faithful for national men’s march, Rosary rally to end abortion
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — There’s still time to join hundreds of faithful in Boston to publicly witness to the unborn at the fifth annual National Men’s March to Abolish Abortion & Rally for Personhood on the solemnity of All Saints. On Sunday, November 1, Catholic men will march three miles from a local Planned Parenthood-Greater Boston Health Center to Boston Common, where a special Rosary Rally that is open to women and children will take place. … Under the new law, an “abortion may be performed by a physician based upon the professional judgment of the physician” and “No medical review process shall override the professional judgment of a treating physician (i.e., abortionist) and a patient or the patient’s health care proxy to provide an abortion consistent with” the new section, effectively empowering abortionists to label any abortion up to birth as “medically necessary.” Faithful who cannot travel to Boston for the march and/or Rosary rally can view the event via the official livestream from Catholics for Catholics, one of the event’s sponsors. Those who are not available to watch the livestream are encouraged to take time to pray for the end of all abortion that day. To register for the event and for more information, click here .

title: Pastor who protested drag queen story time found guilty in retrial
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — More than two years after being acquitted of charges relating to protesting a “drag queen story hour” event marketed to children at a public library, Canadian pastor Derek Reimer was found guilty of mischief and causing a disturbance after a retrial that came from an appeal, but he has vowed to continue the “Lord’s” work. Last Friday in a Calgary, Alberta, courthouse, Reimer was handed the news of his new verdict, which relates to a 2023 incident at the Seton Library. As reported by LifeSiteNews, a judge in 2024 acquitted him of criminal charges for protesting a “drag queen story time” event for children at a public library. … Reimer is now looking at a sentence on both charges as a result of the acquittal. The Democracy Fund has provided assistance, with defense lawyer Alain Hepner noting that another appeal may in the works. In 2025, Reimer was released from jail after earlier in the month being arrested for refusing to comply with a court order mandating he write a formal apology to the Calgary Public Library manager after criticizing him for promoting the “drag queen story hour” for children. Reimer has been in trouble many times for speaking out against the LGBT agenda targeting kids in public spaces.

title: Pakistani court orders reopening of investigation into Christian girl’s abduction
description: ISLAMABAD ( ADF International ) – A high court in Pakistan has ordered that a police investigation be reopened in the case of Maria Shahbaz, a 13-year-old Christian girl who was kidnapped, forced to convert to Islam, and “married” to her 30-year-old abductor, Shehryar Ahmad. A district court had previously accepted an investigation closure report in March. The petition, filed by the family before the High Court, noted that the police allegedly withheld material evidence that Shahbaz’s age was falsified on forged marriage and conversion documents. … ADF has supported dozens of girls who have suffered these abuses. Reeha Saleem was 16 years old when she was abducted by her neighbour while on her way home from school in the Gujrat district. She was taken to an unknown location by four men, subjected to violence and forcibly “married” to one of her captors. After two months of abuse, she was able to flee — yet, since she remained formally “married” to her abuser, the police refused to protect her. Her “marriage” was ultimately annulled by a co In another case, 14-year-old Maira was forcibly “married” and converted from her Christian faith. She escaped her captor, but not before he brutalised, blackmailed, and attempted to forcibly convert her — and when she sought justice, a high court initially ordered that she be returned to her abductor. With legal support from Alliance Defending Freedom, she was ultimately freed from the coerced “marriage” and returned safely to her family. Recently, Pakistan has begun to take notable steps to address this crisis. This year, Punjab — Pakistan’s largest province — passed the Punjab Child Marriage Restraint Act, setting the minimum age for marriage at 18 years.
